summary: Flame in Freefall is a dashboard that makes NASA's microgravity combustion experiments easier to use for fire safety on the Moon and Mars. You choose a scenario (gravity, oxygen, pressure and airflow) and the app ranks 19 NASA PSI investigations by relevance, draws an illustrative flame that reacts to your settings, and shows what nobody has measured yet. That gap is the main finding: all 19 investigations ran in microgravity, so none covers gravity between 0 g and 1 g, the range of the Moon (0.16 g) and Mars (0.38 g). An AI Copilot built on Google Gemini answers questions and sets the scenario, but our code checks every record id and number against the source data and answers "no data" when there is none. Empty cells stay empty: we never estimate values.
details:
Flame in Freefall helps people who plan fire safety for the Moon and Mars see what NASA's microgravity combustion experiments can and cannot tell them.

How it works

You set a scenario: gravity (Earth, Mars, Moon or microgravity), oxygen, pressure and airflow. The app ranks the 19 NASA PSI investigations in our table with a relevance score. The score is our own model, and its weights are declared in the code: gravity 30, oxygen 25, pressure 15, airflow 10, raw data 10, safety areas 10. Missing data scores 0. The flame in the Flame Lab changes with the scenario, but it is an illustration, not a physical simulation.

The Gaps tab shows what the experiments did not cover. All 19 investigations are in microgravity, so there is nothing between 0 g and 1 g. Oxygen, pressure and airflow values exist for only some of them, and the rest stay empty. The Compare tab puts investigations side by side, and the Real data tab shows original NASA tables only when they are real.

The AI Copilot

The Copilot uses Google Gemini to answer questions and to set the scenario ("Show me Mars with 30% oxygen"). The model proposes and the code decides: record ids must exist, numbers must appear in the cited records, a rejected answer is retried, and if the AI is unreachable the app uses pre-checked answers. Where the data does not exist, the Copilot says so.

Data

Each row of the experiments table is one PSI investigation, with its DOI, platform and test conditions taken from the PSI pages. Oxygen, pressure and airflow come from the PSI tables and from NTRS papers, and the source sentence is quoted next to each value. Everything shown carries a label: REAL, MODEL, ILLUSTRATIVE or NO DATA.

What we considered

The risk with a tool like this is a confident answer built on missing data. So the table keeps empty cells empty, the score is labelled as a model, and the AI cannot add numbers of its own.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, pandas, Plotly, pydantic, google-genai, requests. Hosted on Streamlit Community Cloud.

Code: https://github.com/Leopardi007AA/flame-in-freefall-nasa

Independent project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
